# Bank Stress Tests and Liquidity Strains

Report 166 | Published 2025-07-06 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2025-7-6/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/166.json)

Fiscal expansion, reserve pressure and relative bank value.

The liquidity sequence and stress-test description hold up. The explicit twelve-month Bitcoin forecast missed substantially. MVRV remains a descriptive valuation heuristic with overlapping observations, and the Turkey analogy overstates the ability to isolate fiscal causation.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

## Analytical tools and charts

- **MVRV versus two-year returns:** Overlapping observations require cycle-aware validation Visual inspection: yes.
- **SOFR and standing repo:** Separate calendar frictions from persistent reserve scarcity Visual inspection: not performed.
- **Bank stress tests:** Conditional modeled solvency, not universal liquidity safety Visual inspection: not performed.
- **FAST Graphs bank comparisons:** Normalize earnings quality and business mix Visual inspection: not performed.

## Framework lessons

- A clear twelve-month forecast must be scored at that horizon.
- Debt dilution is an accounting outcome; its policy causes require separate evidence.

## Verification limitations

- Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
- Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
